text:
alex: FYI support ticket from a customer hitting 429 mid-stream on SSE. They see partial outputs then connection closed. Customer reports token counters on their dashboard jump dramatically mid-request.

alex: pasted their repro:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \n  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate?model=open-large&stream=true&max_tokens=2048"
```

alex: they say response starts streaming fine, then after ~30s we send a 429 with a small JSON error chunk and connection closes. Client reconnect logic then double-charges tokens (per customer).

maria: @alex can you share the raw server logs for that request_id? request_id from client is 2b8f3a4f

alex: here's snippet from proxy logs (redacted):
```
[2026-02-24T15:12:03Z] INF request_id=2b8f3a4f client=acme-prod start stream
[2026-02-24T15:12:35Z] WRN request_id=2b8f3a4f rate_limiter=burst_check exceeded tokens=120345 limit=100000
[2026-02-24T15:12:35Z] INF request_id=2b8f3a4f send 429 midstream body="{\\"error\\":\\"rate limit\\"}"
[2026-02-24T15:12:35Z] INF request_id=2b8f3a4f connection closed by server
```

jordan: looks like the rate limiter tripped while we were streaming. Why would the token count jump mid-stream? We should be doing progressive accounting, not counting entire predicted tokens up front.

eng-sre-bot: NOTE: a config change to streaming rate-limit accounting was deployed yesterday at 03:04 UTC (changeet #4521) to improve short-request throughput.

maria: @eng-runtime @jordan any recent changes to how we account for streamed tokens? We had a bug a while back where chunked outputs were counted twice if client reconnected.

eng-runtime: We landed a micro-optimization to pre-reserve tokens at stream start and then increment on each chunk. There's an edge-case: if pre-reserve fails we still increment on chunks, which can double-count. That code path was added in PR 4679.

jordan: that matches. If pre-reserve succeeded and then chunk increments also ran, ledger would show both pre-reserve + per-chunk. For long streams that can exceed quota mid-stream, causing 429 mid-stream.

alex: customer also says their invoice shows the extra tokens and they opened a billing escalation. @billing can you confirm?

billing: Confirmed — sample customer ledger lines for that account show: 
```
2026-02-24T15:12:03 request_id=2b8f3a4f reserved=100000
2026-02-24T15:12:35 request_id=2b8f3a4f incremented=20345
```
Billing: So we charged reserved + increments = 120345 tokens. Looks wrong for a single request.

maria: Ok we need an immediate mitigation and a long-term fix. Mitigation options:
- revert the pre-reserve + per-chunk double-path (safe rollback)
- make client-facing change: return Retry-After header and keep connection open with 503 instead of hard 429 mid-stream (not ideal)
- add server-side detect to disable pre-reserve when chunk accounting enabled

jordan: I can assemble a quick patch to short-circuit the pre-reserve when streaming flag is set. Will test on staging.

alex: Customer wants repro steps we can run internally. I left their exact curl above. Also added note: "client sees partial JSON events then a final SSE event: data: {\"error\":\"429\"}"

maria: Repro instructions for eng: run a long generate with small chunking interval. Example client sim (node):
```js
// simulate long streaming generation that would cross preset quotas
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate?stream=true', {
  headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer <TEST_KEY>' },
  method: 'POST',
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'open-large', prompt: 'long prompt', max_tokens: 2000 }),
});
res.body.on('data', (chunk) => console.log(chunk.toString()));
```

eng-runtime: I pulled staging logs and reproduced with the patched pre-reserve disabled — no 429 mid-stream, ledger shows only the increments. So patch works.

jordan: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4720 — short-circuits pre-reserve when stream=true. Running CI, will roll to canary.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: canary/serving v2026.02.24-4720 -> region-us-dev (2 nodes)

eng-sre-bot: Canary metrics: 0.2% increased tail latency, but 0 mid-stream 429s observed in test window.

alex: I asked customer to try again with a temporary key (we gave them test key tied to sandbox quotas) to confirm behavior; they tried and reported: "looks good — full stream, no abrupt 429, token count looks reasonable" :thumbsup:

billing: We issued a provisional credit for the overcharged tokens and will follow up with acct manager.

maria: Follow-ups:
- jordan to finish full fix and add unit tests for pre-reserve/stream accounting (blocking race), include regression test that simulates client reconnects.
- eng-runtime to audit other changes that touch quota accounting in last 30 days.
- support to confirm with customer in 24h and close the ticket if all good.

jordan: I'll add logs and a metric (counter) for "pre_reserve_taken" vs "chunk_increments" per request so we can alert if both occur.

alex: Customer confirmed again at 2026-02-24T17:05:11 — closing on their end. Marking as resolved here pending postmortem.

maria: filing a brief postmortem with timeline + root cause (race between pre-reserve and per-chunk increment leading to double accounting) and remediation (rollback + unit tests + metric + billing credits).

eng-runtime: PR merged and rolled to prod by noon UTC.

deploy-bot: Deploy complete: serving v2026.02.24-4720 -> region-us (all clusters) :white_check_mark:

maria: Thanks team. leaving P0 label until postmortem is posted.

alex: tagging this resolved in thread. If customer reopens we'll rehydrate.

eng-sre-bot: ACTIONS: create alert if (pre_reserve_taken && chunk_increments > 0) per request id.

alex: closing. :lock:
